questions.question: Critically examine bell hooks's narrative about her personal experiences with lack of love. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Hooks explores her childhood experience where physical care was provided, but
  • emotional love and affirmation were missing. She examines how traditional,
  • authoritarian family structures often prioritize obedience and control over genuine
  • emotional bonding. The narrative highlights how society often lacks a "love ethic,"
  • leading to a culture of domination rather than mutual respect. Her personal struggle
  • serves as a critique, suggesting that recognizing the absence of love is the first step
  • toward reclaiming it. (K/CO1)

questions.question: How does Crime and Punishment explore the conflict between intellectualism and spirituality? / [CO2] [15x1 = 15]
questions.solution_html:
• Raskolnikov’s "Extraordinary Man" theory uses cold, mathematical logic to justify
  • murder for a supposed "greater good". Sonya Marmeladov represents pure spirituality,
  • redemption, and the Christian ideal of suffering for others. The protagonist’s mental
  • and physical breakdown illustrates that human nature and morality cannot be reduced
  • to intellectual theories. The conflict is resolved when Raskolnikov abandons his
  • prideful intellectualism to accept Sonya’s path of spiritual humility and "New Life".
  • (U/CO2)
